name: Polaroid Corp. v. Polarad Electronics Corp.
summary: The Second Circuit established an eight-factor balancing test to determine likelihood of trademark confusion, considering factors such as the strength of the mark, similarity of the marks, and sophistication of buyers.
significance: The Second Circuit's multi-factor likelihood-of-confusion test from this case governs how courts in that circuit evaluate whether two marks are likely to confuse consumers, and its application is central to the dispute.
